definition: An educational LUNAFORGE Earth-observation mission scenario focused on simulated observations of the Nile Delta.
The removal of material from a coast, which can cause the shoreline to move landward over time.
The accumulation of sediment along a coast, which can cause the shoreline to move seaward.
A change in the position or shape of a shoreline over time. Different parts of the Nile Delta can experience erosion, accretion, or relative stability.
An area where water covers or saturates the soil for at least part of the year, supporting water-adapted plants and wildlife.
The physical material or surface present on the ground, such as water, vegetation, bare soil, or buildings.
A change in how people use an area of land, such as converting agricultural fields into built-up areas.
A family of Earth-observation satellites that collect images used to study land and environmental change.
A European Copernicus satellite mission that provides multispectral optical imagery of Earth's land and coastal areas.
The approximate ground dimension represented by one image pixel. It is commonly expressed in metres per pixel and depends on the imaging system and observation geometry.
Artificially generated values or images used by a simulation. They are not measurements collected by a real satellite.
The transmission of stored spacecraft data to a ground station.
